feat(sources/community/huggingface): add Hugging Face community source (#465)

## Summary

Adds a new community source for Hugging Face under
`sources/community/huggingface/`.

This source enables querying Hugging Face Hub data (models, datasets,
Spaces, daily papers, and trending repos) through SQL using the [Hub
REST API](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/api). The source is
manifest-only, read-only, and uses Coral's existing HTTP source-spec
model. No CLI, MCP, config, or runtime changes.

Closes #464

## What changed

Added:
- `sources/community/huggingface/manifest.yaml` (~1010 lines)
- `sources/community/huggingface/README.md` (~240 lines)

## Tables

| Table | Endpoint | Pagination | Filters | Columns |
|-------|----------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `models` | `GET /api/models?full=true` | `link_header` (100/page) | 6
optional | 20 |
| `datasets` | `GET /api/datasets?full=true` | `link_header` (100/page)
| 5 optional | 18 |
| `spaces` | `GET /api/spaces?full=true` | `link_header` (100/page) | 5
optional | 18 |
| `daily_papers` | `GET /api/daily_papers` | `none` (up to 100 recent) |
— | 17 |
| `trending` | `GET /api/trending` | `none` (up to 60 items) | 1
optional | 12 |

## Auth

Bearer token via `Authorization: Bearer <HF_TOKEN>`.

Inputs:
- `HF_TOKEN` — required secret, created at
[huggingface.co/settings/tokens](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens)
with at least `read` scope. A read-only token is sufficient for all
tables.

## Implementation notes

### Pagination

- **`link_header` for models/datasets/spaces** — the Hub API uses
standard RFC Link headers with `rel="next"` for cursor-based pagination.
These tables use 100 items per page.
- **`mode: none` for daily_papers** — the daily papers API paginates
through the full historical archive via `rel="next"`. Using
`link_header` here causes unbounded fetches for client-side filters
(e.g. `IS NOT NULL`). Changed to `mode: none` which returns up to 100
recent papers in a single bounded request.
- **`mode: none` for trending** — returns up to 60 items (20 models + 20
datasets + 20 spaces). The Hub API rejects `limit > 20`.

### Response mapping

- **Top-level JSON arrays** — listing endpoints return flat JSON arrays,
so `rows_path: []` is used.
- **Full metadata mode** — listing endpoints use `full=true` to include
`author`, `sha`, `gated`, `disabled`, `lastModified`, `cardData`, and
`siblings`.
- **Trending response structure** — returns `{ recentlyTrending: [...]
}` with repo data nested under `repoData` and author data under
`repoData.authorData`.

### Columns

- **Json-typed columns** for structured data:
- `siblings` (models, datasets, spaces) — repository file listing with
`rfilename` entries
- `card_data` (datasets, spaces) — full card YAML metadata including
license, language, task categories, sdk config
  - `authors` (daily_papers) — array of paper author objects
- **Nested field flattening with `__` separator**:
- Daily papers: `submitted_by__user`, `submitted_by__fullname`,
`organization__name`, `organization__fullname`
  - Trending: `author__name`, `author__fullname`, `author__type`
- **AI-generated paper metadata** — `ai_summary` (one-sentence overview)
and `ai_keywords` (comma-separated via `join_array`)
- **Tags as comma-separated strings** via `join_array` expressions

### Filters

- **Virtual `from_filter` columns match filter names** — `search`,
`filter`, `sort`, `direction`, `type` are virtual columns named to match
their filter keys, so `WHERE search = 'llama'` works directly in SQL.
- **Tag-based filtering** — framework filtering uses `WHERE filter =
'transformers'`, not a separate `library` param (the HF API ignores
`library` as a query param).
- **Sort direction** — only descending (`-1`) is reliably supported; the
HF API rejects ascending for some fields like `downloads`.
- **Models** support 6 optional filters: `search`, `author`,
`pipeline_tag`, `filter`, `sort`, `direction`
- **Datasets/Spaces** support 5 each: `search`, `author`, `filter`,
`sort`, `direction`
- **Trending** supports 1: `type` (model, dataset, or space)
- **Gated field as Utf8** — the API returns either `false` (boolean) or
`"auto"` / `"manual"` (string)

## Validation

- `coral source lint` — **passes**
- `make lint-sources` (`ryl`) — **passes**
- `git diff --check` — **passes**
- `coral source add` — **passes**
- `coral source test huggingface` — **4 declared, 4 passed**

Live Coral queries tested:

```sql
-- ✅ models (basic)
SELECT id, pipeline_tag, likes, downloads FROM huggingface.models LIMIT 1;

-- ✅ models (search filter)
SELECT id, likes FROM huggingface.models WHERE search = 'llama' LIMIT 5;

-- ✅ models (tag filter)
SELECT id, author FROM huggingface.models WHERE filter = 'transformers' LIMIT 5;

-- ✅ models (pipeline_tag filter)
SELECT id, likes FROM huggingface.models WHERE pipeline_tag = 'text-generation' LIMIT 5;

-- ✅ models (author filter)
SELECT id, pipeline_tag FROM huggingface.models WHERE author = 'meta-llama';

-- ✅ datasets (basic)
SELECT id, likes, downloads FROM huggingface.datasets LIMIT 1;

-- ✅ datasets (search filter)
SELECT id, likes FROM huggingface.datasets WHERE search = 'code' LIMIT 5;

-- ✅ spaces (basic + filter)
SELECT id, sdk, likes FROM huggingface.spaces WHERE filter = 'gradio' LIMIT 5;

-- ✅ spaces (mcp-server filter)
SELECT id, author FROM huggingface.spaces WHERE filter = 'mcp-server' LIMIT 5;

-- ✅ daily_papers (basic)
SELECT paper_id, title, ai_summary FROM huggingface.daily_papers LIMIT 10;

-- ✅ trending (basic)
SELECT repo_id, repo_type, likes FROM huggingface.trending;

-- ✅ trending (type filter)
SELECT repo_id, likes FROM huggingface.trending WHERE type = 'model';
```

Live API responses confirmed correct field mapping for all 5 endpoints.

## User-visible impact

New `huggingface` source installable via:

```bash
coral source add --file sources/community/huggingface/manifest.yaml
```

## Known limitations

- **Read-only** — no create, update, or delete operations.
- **Rate limits** — the Hub API has rate limits that depend on account
tier. See [rate limits
docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/rate-limits).
- **Tags as strings** — use SQL `LIKE` to filter by tag.
- **Gated field** — typed as `Utf8` because the API returns `false`,
`"auto"`, or `"manual"`.
- **Daily papers scope** — returns up to 100 recent papers per query
without pagination. Client-side filters (e.g. `IS NOT NULL`) work within
that batch.
- **No repo-level detail** — Hub-level listing and discovery only.
- **Trending scope** — Hub's curated list: 60 items unfiltered, 20 per
type.
- **Sort direction** — ascending is not supported for all sort fields.

## Out of scope

Not included in v1:
- Single-model/dataset/space detail lookups (`/api/models/{id}`)
- File tree and commit history
- Discussions and pull requests
- Organization management (members, billing, settings)
- Inference API endpoints
- Write operations (repo creation, file uploads)
- Webhook management

feat(sources/community/honeycomb): add Honeycomb community source (#463)

## Summary

Adds a new community source for Honeycomb under
`sources/community/honeycomb/`.

This source enables querying Honeycomb observability platform metadata
(datasets, columns, boards, markers, and triggers) through SQL using
Honeycomb's Configuration API (v1). The source is manifest-only,
read-only, and uses Coral's existing HTTP source-spec model with simple
REST GET endpoints. No CLI, MCP, config, or runtime changes.

Closes #462

## What changed

**Added:**

- `sources/community/honeycomb/manifest.yaml`
- `sources/community/honeycomb/README.md`

### Tables

| Table | Endpoint | Required Filters | Pagination |
|-------|----------|------------------|------------|
| `datasets` | `GET /datasets` | — | none |
| `columns` | `GET /columns/{datasetSlug}` | `dataset_slug` | none |
| `boards` | `GET /boards` | — | none |
| `markers` | `GET /markers/{datasetSlug}` | `dataset_slug` | none |
| `triggers` | `GET /triggers/{datasetSlug}` | `dataset_slug` | none |

### Auth

Custom header via `X-Honeycomb-Team: <HONEYCOMB_API_KEY>`.

**Inputs:**

- `HONEYCOMB_API_KEY` required secret, a Honeycomb Configuration Key
(prefix `hcxlk_`). Created at Environment Settings → API Keys →
Configuration tab. Requires read access to datasets, columns, boards,
markers, and triggers.
- `HONEYCOMB_API_BASE` optional variable, defaults to
`https://api.honeycomb.io/1`. Set to `https://api.eu1.honeycomb.io/1`
for EU environments.

## Implementation notes

- **REST over HTTP** all tables use `method: GET` against Honeycomb's v1
Configuration API at `https://api.honeycomb.io/1`. Filter values are
injected directly into URL path segments via `{{filter.dataset_slug}}`.
- **No pagination** all v1 list endpoints return the complete result set
in a single top-level JSON array. The Honeycomb [pagination
docs](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/pagination/) confirm that only three
`/2/` endpoints are paginated, none of which are used by this source.
- **`row_strategy: direct`** all responses are top-level JSON arrays
(`[{...}, {...}]`), so the default `direct` strategy works with an empty
`response: {}` block.
- **Custom auth header** Honeycomb uses `X-Honeycomb-Team` instead of
the standard `Authorization` header. The manifest uses `HeaderAuth` with
`from: input` to inject the Configuration Key into this custom header.
- **`from_filter` virtual columns** the `columns`, `markers`, and
`triggers` tables echo the `dataset_slug` filter value back into result
rows for traceability. In the `triggers` table, this column is named
`dataset_slug_filter` to avoid collision with the API's own
`dataset_slug` response field.
- **ISO 8601 timestamps** all timestamp fields (`created_at`,
`updated_at`, `last_written_at`, `last_written`) use `type: Timestamp`
with `format_timestamp` / `input: iso8601`. Marker `start_time` and
`end_time` are Unix epoch integers and use `type: Int64` instead.
- **Complex nested structures as Json** board `panels`, `tags`, and
`preset_filters`; trigger `threshold`, `query`, `recipients`, `tags`,
`evaluation_schedule`, and `baseline_details` are preserved as `type:
Json` columns.
- **Renamed API fields** the API returns a generic `type` field on
boards, markers, and triggers. These are renamed to `board_type`,
`marker_type`, and `alert_type` respectively for SQL clarity and to
avoid reserved word conflicts.
- **`__all__` slug support** the `columns`, `markers`, and `triggers`
tables document that users can pass `'__all__'` as the `dataset_slug`
filter to query across all datasets in the environment (not available
for Classic environments).
- **EU region support** the `HONEYCOMB_API_BASE` variable allows
overriding the base URL for EU-hosted Honeycomb environments.

## Validation

- `coral source lint sources/community/honeycomb/manifest.yaml`
**passes** (`Manifest is valid`)
- Live query validation was not completed because it requires a real
`HONEYCOMB_API_KEY`. The manifest structure and column mappings have
been validated against the official [Honeycomb Configuration API
documentation](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/).

## User-visible impact

New `honeycomb` source installable via:

```sh
coral source add --file sources/community/honeycomb/manifest.yaml
```

**Example queries:**

```sql
-- List all datasets and their column counts
SELECT name, slug, regular_columns_count, created_at
  FROM honeycomb.datasets
 ORDER BY created_at DESC;

-- Inspect columns in a specific dataset
SELECT key_name, type, hidden, last_written
  FROM honeycomb.columns
 WHERE dataset_slug = 'my-dataset';

-- Find all columns across the environment
SELECT key_name, type, description
  FROM honeycomb.columns
 WHERE dataset_slug = '__all__';

-- List all boards
SELECT name, description, board_type
  FROM honeycomb.boards;

-- Find recent deployment markers
SELECT id, message, marker_type, start_time
  FROM honeycomb.markers
 WHERE dataset_slug = '__all__';

-- Find triggers that are currently firing
SELECT name, alert_type, triggered, disabled
  FROM honeycomb.triggers
 WHERE dataset_slug = '__all__';
```

## Known limitations

- **Configuration Keys only** Ingest Keys (`hcxik_`) and Management Keys
(`hcxmk_`) are not supported. Only Configuration Keys (`hcxlk_`) work
with the v1 Configuration API.
- **Secret boards excluded** the boards endpoint returns only non-secret
boards. There is no API to list secret boards with a Configuration Key.
- **No pagination** if an environment has a very large number of
datasets, columns, or triggers, all items are returned in a single
response. This is a v1 API design limitation.
- **Marker timestamps are Unix integers** `start_time` and `end_time`
are `Int64` (Unix epoch seconds), not `Timestamp`, because the API
returns them as raw integers rather than ISO 8601 strings.
- **Classic environments** the `__all__` dataset slug is not supported
on Honeycomb Classic. Users must specify individual dataset slugs.
- **Read-only** no create, update, or delete operations.

## Out of scope

Not included in v1:

- Active query execution and result retrieval
- SLO management and burn alerts
- Derived columns and calculated fields
- Marker settings (color/type management)
- Team management (`/2/` Management API endpoints)
- Environment and API key management
- Write operations (create dataset, create trigger, etc.)
- Recipient management and notification configuration

feat(sources/community/resend): add Resend community source (#500)

## Summary

Adds a new community source for Resend under
`sources/community/resend/`.

This source enables querying Resend account data (sent emails, domains,
API keys, contacts, segments, broadcasts, topics, webhooks, and API
request logs) through SQL using the Resend REST API. The source is
manifest-only, read-only, and uses Coral's existing HTTP source-spec
model with `HeaderAuth`. No CLI, MCP, config, or runtime changes.

Closes #499 

## What changed

Added:

- `sources/community/resend/manifest.yaml`
- `sources/community/resend/README.md`

## Tables

| Table | Endpoint | Required Filters | Pagination | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `emails` | `GET /emails` | — | none (first 100) | Sent emails with
delivery status |
| `domains` | `GET /domains` | — | none (first 100) | Domain
verification, region, capabilities |
| `api_keys` | `GET /api-keys` | — | none | API key metadata (no key
values) |
| `audiences` | `GET /audiences` | — | none | Legacy audiences (backward
compat) |
| `segments` | `GET /segments` | — | none (first 100) | Contact segments
for broadcast targeting |
| `contacts` | `GET /contacts` | — | none (first 100) | Global contacts
with subscription status |
| `broadcasts` | `GET /broadcasts` | — | none | Bulk email campaigns
with status |
| `topics` | `GET /topics` | — | none (first 100) | Subscription
preference topics |
| `webhooks` | `GET /webhooks` | — | none | Webhook endpoints and
subscribed events |
| `logs` | `GET /logs` | — | none (first 100) | API request audit trail
|

## Auth

Bearer token authentication with `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`.

Inputs:

- `RESEND_API_KEY` — required secret. Resend API key (starts with
`re_`). Create at https://resend.com/api-keys. **Must have Full access
permission** — Sending-only keys cannot read data and will return 401
`restricted_api_key`.

## Implementation notes

- All list endpoints return a standard envelope: `{"object": "list",
"has_more": bool, "data": [...]}`. All tables use `rows_path: [data]`
- Pagination is set to `mode: none` because Resend uses item-ID cursor
pagination (`after`/`before` query params where the cursor is the last
row's UUID). Coral's `response_cursor_path` reads from a fixed JSON path
and cannot extract the last array element's `id`. Each table returns the
first page (up to 100 items).
- Contacts use the current global `GET /contacts` endpoint, not the
legacy audience-scoped `GET /audiences/:id/contacts`
- `audiences` is kept as a legacy table alongside `segments` for
accounts that haven't migrated
- `segments` and `topics` tables are included so `broadcasts.segment_id`
and `broadcasts.topic_id` are resolvable via JOINs
- The `from` column in `emails` is a reserved SQL keyword — documented
that users must double-quote it (`"from"`)
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 strings mapped as `Utf8` (varying timezone
formats: `+00:00` vs `Z`)
- Multi-value fields (`to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `reply_to` in emails; `events`
in webhooks; `capabilities` in domains) are mapped as `Json`
- API key values are never returned by the Resend API; the `api_keys`
table only exposes metadata (name, creation time, last used)
- Rate limit is 5 requests per second per team (Resend default)

## Validation

- `coral source lint sources/community/resend/manifest.yaml` — passes
- `make lint-sources` — passes with no warnings
- `git diff --check` — passes
- `coral source add` with full-access key — successfully exposes 10
tables, test query passes
- Live query validation — **all 10 tables queried successfully** with a
real Resend API key:
- `api_keys`: 2 rows returned (coral-full, Onboarding) with all 4
columns populated correctly
  - `audiences`: 1 row returned (General) with id, name, created_at
  - `segments`: 1 row returned (General) with id, name, created_at
- `logs`: 5 rows returned showing Coral's own API requests with
endpoint, method, response_status (200), user_agent (coral/0.2.1),
created_at
- `domains`, `emails`, `contacts`, `broadcasts`, `topics`, `webhooks`: 0
rows (new account, no data configured) — proper empty results, correct
column headers, no errors

## User-visible impact

New `resend` source installable via:

```bash
export RESEND_API_KEY="re_your_full_access_key"
coral source add --file sources/community/resend/manifest.yaml
```

Example queries:

```sql
-- Review recent email delivery status
SELECT id, "from", subject, last_event, created_at
FROM resend.emails
LIMIT 20;

-- List all domains with verification state
SELECT id, name, status, region, capabilities
FROM resend.domains;

-- Audit API key usage
SELECT name, created_at, last_used_at
FROM resend.api_keys;

-- List contacts with subscription status
SELECT email, first_name, last_name, unsubscribed
FROM resend.contacts
LIMIT 20;

-- Review broadcast campaigns
SELECT id, status, segment_id, topic_id, scheduled_at, sent_at
FROM resend.broadcasts;

-- Resolve segments and topics for broadcasts
SELECT id, name, created_at FROM resend.segments;
SELECT id, name, default_subscription, visibility FROM resend.topics;

-- Audit webhooks
SELECT endpoint, status, events, created_at
FROM resend.webhooks;

-- Check API error rates from logs
SELECT endpoint, method, response_status, user_agent, created_at
FROM resend.logs
WHERE response_status >= 400
LIMIT 20;

-- Find bounced emails
SELECT id, "from", subject, created_at
FROM resend.emails
WHERE last_event = 'bounced';

-- Check unsubscribed contacts
SELECT email, first_name, last_name, created_at
FROM resend.contacts
WHERE unsubscribed = true;
```

## Known limitations

- **Read-only** — no send, create, update, or delete operations
- **First-page only** — cursor pagination cannot be expressed with
`response_cursor_path`, so each table returns at most 100 items
- **`from` is reserved** — the `from` column in `emails` must be
double-quoted in SQL
- **Timestamps as strings** — ISO 8601 format strings, not `Timestamp`
type
- **Full access key required** — Sending-only API keys return 401 on all
GET endpoints

## Out of scope

Not included in v1:

- Received emails (`GET /emails/received`)
- Automations and automation runs
- Custom events
- Email templates
- Contact properties (custom metadata)
- Segment contacts (per-segment contact list)
- Write operations (send, create, update, delete)
- Cursor pagination for large email/contact lists

## Summary

Adds a new community source for Milvus under
`sources/community/milvus/`.

This source enables querying Milvus vector database metadata, collection
schemas, partition layouts, aliases, authentication metadata, and
retrieval infrastructure through SQL using Coral.

The source is designed for:

- vector infrastructure visibility
- AI retrieval governance
- operational metadata auditing
- RAG infrastructure discovery
- semantic search infrastructure analysis

The implementation is intentionally:

- read-only
- metadata-focused
- operationally scoped
- lightweight
- easy to validate locally

Supports:

- local/self-hosted Milvus standalone deployments
- distributed/self-hosted Milvus clusters
- Zilliz Cloud deployments

---

## Tables (9)

| Table | Description |
|---|---|
| databases | Lists all databases in the Milvus instance; start here to
discover `database_name` values for scoped queries |
| collections | Lists collection identifiers within a database; optional
`db_name` filter (defaults to `"default"`); use `collection_name` values
to drive `collection_details` and `partitions` |
| collection_details | Full schema and configuration for a specific
collection including field definitions, index configs, load state, shard
count, consistency level, and dynamic field support; requires
`collection_name` |
| collection_stats | Row count for a specific collection |
| partitions | Partitions within a collection; requires
`collection_name`; optional `db_name`; the default partition is always
`_default` |
| users | Usernames in the internal Milvus auth database; requires admin
privileges on the instance |
| roles | Roles defined in the instance; default roles are `admin` and
`public` |
| aliases | Collection aliases; optional `db_name` filter |

---

## Auth

Authentication uses Bearer token auth via:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

Configured through:

```env
MILVUS_TOKEN
MILVUS_URL
```

### Supported auth modes

#### No-auth local instance

Use any non-empty placeholder:

```env
MILVUS_TOKEN=none
```

#### Username/password auth

```env
MILVUS_TOKEN=username:password
```

#### Zilliz Cloud

Use the API key directly:

```env
MILVUS_TOKEN=<api-key>
```

### Default local URL

The source defaults to:

```env
MILVUS_URL=http://localhost:19530
```

Override as needed for remote/self-hosted clusters or Zilliz Cloud
deployments.

```env

```

```env

```

Milvus is one of the most widely deployed open-source vector databases
used heavily in:

- RAG pipelines
- semantic search
- AI-native applications
- recommendation systems
- embedding retrieval workflows
- large-scale vector search systems

Teams often need operational visibility into:

- which collections exist
- collection schema layouts
- embedding field definitions
- vector index configurations
- partition organization
- alias mappings
- authentication and role metadata

Without a Coral source, users typically need to:

- manually inspect Attu or Milvus dashboards
- query Milvus APIs directly
- maintain custom metadata scripts
- export vector infrastructure metadata separately
- correlate retrieval infrastructure manually

Being able to query vector infrastructure metadata directly through SQL
is a natural fit for Coral AI infrastructure visibility, governance
workflows, and operational retrieval analytics.

  - returns collection identifiers scoped to the default database

- `collections` with `db_name` filter
  - correctly scopes to the specified database

- `collection_details`
  - returns schema with:
    - fields as JSON columns
    - indexes as JSON columns
    - load state
    - consistency level
    - dynamic field flag

- `partitions`
  - returns partition metadata for the given collection

- `users`
  - returns usernames from the internal auth database

- `roles`
  - returns `admin` and `public` default roles

- `aliases`
  - returns empty result set on a fresh instance (correct behavior)

---

## User-visible impact

New `milvus` source installable via:

```bash
MILVUS_TOKEN=none \
coral source add --file sources/community/milvus/manifest.yaml
```

Or interactively:

```bash
MILVUS_TOKEN=none \
coral source add --file sources/community/milvus/manifest.yaml --interactive
```

---

## Example queries

### List databases

```sql
SELECT database_name
FROM milvus.databases
```

### List collections in the default database

```sql
SELECT collection_name, db_name
FROM milvus.collections
LIMIT 20
```

### Inspect collection schema and metadata

```sql
SELECT collection_name, fields, indexes, load_state
FROM milvus.collection_details
WHERE collection_name = 'example_collection'
```

### List partitions for a collection

```sql
SELECT partition_name, collection_name
FROM milvus.partitions
WHERE collection_name = 'example_collection'
```

### Get the row count for a collection

```sql
SELECT row_count
FROM milvus.collection_stats
WHERE collection_name = 'my_collection'
```

### List aliases configured in a database

```sql
SELECT alias_name, db_name
FROM milvus.aliases
```

---

## Implementation notes

- Source intentionally remains read-only in v1
- Nested provider payloads are preserved as JSON where appropriate
- `fields` and `indexes` are currently exposed as raw JSON structures
from the upstream API
- Supports local, distributed, and cloud Milvus deployments
- Designed for operational metadata visibility rather than vector
querying
- Avoids collection mutations, vector insertion, and similarity search
execution APIs
- `collection_stats` table (`POST /v2/vectordb/collections/get_stats`)
for row count and storage size per collection

---

## Follow-on

Potential future additions:

- normalized `indexes` table for operational index analytics
(`metric_type`, `index_type`, etc.)
- normalized `collection_fields` table for embedding/vector field
discovery
- `alias_details` table backed by `aliases/describe` to map aliases to
target collections
- `role_privileges` table (`POST /v2/vectordb/roles/describe`) to
surface per-role privilege grants
- `user_roles` table to map users to their assigned roles
- distributed cluster metadata tables
- query metrics and retrieval performance metadata

Changes:

that returns ranked candidate rows and must carry `search_limits`.

working, add `kind: search` functions for provider search endpoints,
guide contributors toward functions, then remove/deprecate
compatibility-table search filters after sources and docs have moved.

feat(catalog)!: expose unified catalog discovery (#459) ## Intent MCP discovery is currently table-shaped. Agents can use `list_tables` and `search_tables`, and they can query table metadata through `coral.tables`. Source-scoped table functions are only discoverable if the agent already knows to query `coral.table_functions`. That means an agent following the normal MCP discovery path can miss function-only capabilities entirely. This PR makes catalog discovery the MCP/API surface for both tables and table functions. The choice is deliberately unified instead of adding separate `list_table_functions` / `search_table_functions` tools: agents can be lazy, and one discovery surface makes it more likely they search the whole queryable catalog. Internal CRAG benchmark comparison supports that shape: | Discovery shape | CRAG score | Accuracy | Hallucination | Missing | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Separate table/function discovery | 0.5041 | 66.67% | 16.26% | 17.07% | | Unified catalog discovery | 0.5528 | 69.11% | 13.82% | 17.07% | MLflow A/B comparison: [run comparison](http://mlflow-bench/#/experiments/19/runs/b2f3d7292c174f3598cb774962ac9c48/evaluations?compareToRunUuid=74adac504c8c424ab8d5dc99ac889d72). Left side is this PR; right side is the comparison run. This PR is stacked on #448 (`james/catalog-discovery-service`) so catalog discovery stays app-owned and MCP remains a thin adapter. Greatly improves table function discovery (left is this PR - right is main): ## What Changed - Add typed table-function metadata to the engine catalog. - Derive `coral.table_functions` from that typed metadata. - Extend app catalog discovery to return catalog items of kind `table` or `table_function`. - Add unified `ListCatalog` / `SearchCatalog` discovery over both item kinds. - Replace MCP table-only discovery with `list_catalog` / `search_catalog`. - Return a common `sql_reference` for catalog items and a `sql_call_example` for table functions. - Make `coral://guide` derive visible schemas from all catalog item kinds so function-only sources are not hidden. ## Ownership / Boundaries - `coral-engine` owns runtime-visible metadata and the `coral.table_functions` system table. - `coral-app` owns workspace-scoped catalog collection, kind filtering, ordering, search, and pagination. - `coral-api` owns the unified wire contract. - `coral-mcp` maps MCP tool arguments/results onto the app catalog API. `list_catalog` and `search_catalog` share one app-level collection path, so table and function discovery cannot drift in source coverage, kind filtering, ordering, or pagination. Table-specific operations remain table-specific where the operation itself is table-specific: `DescribeTable`, `ListColumns`, and SQL over `coral.tables`. ## Compatibility / User Impact This is an intentional breaking MCP/API discovery-surface change. - Public MCP `list_tables` / `search_tables` are replaced by `list_catalog` / `search_catalog`. - Table-only/table-function-only gRPC discovery RPCs are not exposed. Callers should use `ListCatalog` / `SearchCatalog` with `kind = CATALOG_ITEM_KIND_TABLE`, `kind = CATALOG_ITEM_KIND_TABLE_FUNCTION`, or the default `CATALOG_ITEM_KIND_UNSPECIFIED`. - MCP response payloads are rendered through named serializable structs and validated against advertised output schemas in integration tests. ## Not in This PR - No separate `list_table_functions` or `search_table_functions` MCP tools. - No table-function describe tool. - No table-function column-list tool. - No SQL execution changes for table functions. - No compatibility aliases for removed MCP tools. ## Validation - `cargo check -p coral-app -p coral-mcp -p coral-cli --features cli-test-server` - `cargo test -p coral-engine list_catalog_collects_tables_and_functions_together` - `cargo test -p coral-app catalog_discovery_tests` - `cargo test -p coral-app --test grpc source_lifecycle_tests::list_catalog_supports_table_kind_and_pagination` - `cargo test -p coral-mcp list_catalog_surfaces_table_functions` - `cargo test -p coral-mcp guide_content_includes_function_only_schemas` - `cargo test -p coral-engine --test engine catalog` - `cargo test -p coral-app --test grpc catalog` - `cargo test -p coral-mcp` - `cargo test -p coral-cli --features cli-test-server --test mcp` - `make docs-check` - `make rust-checks`

feat(sources/community/kafka): add Apache Kafka source (#550)

Closes #528

## Summary

Adds a community source for Apache Kafka under
`sources/community/kafka/`.

Pivoted from Kafka UI (`provectuslabs/kafka-ui`) to the
[Confluent Kafka REST Proxy](https://github.com/confluentinc/kafka-rest)
as the HTTP bridge, per reviewer feedback that it is the most widely
adopted
standard bridge for Kafka.

---

## Why the pivot

| Feature | Kafka UI (provectuslabs) | Confluent Kafka REST Proxy |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol | Proprietary REST API | Open standard (v3 Admin API) |
| Adoption | Moderate — UI-focused tool | Industry standard HTTP bridge
|
| Maintained by | Community | Confluent (Kafka creators) |
| Default port | 8080 | 8082 |
| Throughput metrics (bytes/sec) | ✅ via JMX polling | ❌ (use
JMX/Prometheus) |
| Broker skew metrics | ✅ | ❌ |
| Topic configs (with source + is_default) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Consumer lag (per-partition) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Open standard / versioned API | ❌ | ✅ |

The REST Proxy is the right foundation — it is the official HTTP bridge
recommended by the Kafka community, ships with Confluent Platform, and
exposes
a clean versioned v3 Admin API that maps directly to the Kafka Admin
Client.

---

## Tables (6)

| Table | Required filters | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cluster` | — | Single row with `cluster_id`. Start here. |
| `brokers` | `cluster_id` | Per-broker host, port, rack. |
| `topics` | `cluster_id` | Topic list with partition count, replication
factor, internal flag. |
| `topic_configs` | `cluster_id`, `topic_name` | Full config key-value
pairs with source and default flag. |
| `consumer_groups` | `cluster_id` | Consumer group state and assignor.
|
| `consumer_group_lags` | `cluster_id`, `group_id` | Per-partition
offset and lag for a consumer group. |

---

## Auth

```
KAFKA_REST_URL   # default: http://localhost:8082
```

No authentication required by default.

---

## Local Setup

```bash
docker network create kafka-net

docker run -d \
  --network kafka-net --name kafka -p 9092:9092 \
  -e KAFKA_NODE_ID=1 \
  -e KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES=broker,controller \
  -e KAFKA_LISTENERS="PLAINTEXT://0.0.0.0:9092,CONTROLLER://0.0.0.0:9093" \
  -e KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS="PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092" \
  -e KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES=CONTROLLER \
  -e KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP="CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT" \
  -e KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS="1@kafka:9093" \
  -e KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR=1 \
  -e KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR=1 \
  -e KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR=1 \
  -e KAFKA_GROUP_INITIAL_REBALANCE_DELAY_MS=0 \
  apache/kafka:latest

docker run -d \
  --network kafka-net --name kafka-rest -p 8082:8082 \
  -e KAFKA_REST_HOST_NAME=kafka-rest \
  -e KAFKA_REST_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=kafka:9092 \
  -e KAFKA_REST_LISTENERS=http://0.0.0.0:8082 \
  confluentinc/cp-kafka-rest:latest
```

Add the source:

```bash
export KAFKA_REST_URL=http://localhost:8082
coral source add --file sources/community/kafka/manifest.yaml
```

refactor(app): split source credential persistence (#324)

## Intent

Move plaintext source credential material out of the general app state boundary and into a dedicated app-owned credentials boundary, while preserving the existing on-disk storage contract.

## What it enables

- Keeps source credential material owned by `crates/coral-app/src/credentials` instead of `state`.
- Introduces `CredentialManager` and `CredentialSetId` so source lifecycle and query loading depend on credential-set operations rather than source-secret store internals.
- Preserves the existing `workspaces/<workspace>/sources/<source>/secrets.env` path and `config.toml` `secrets` key behavior.
- Handles credential replacement without parsing malformed existing material, and keeps rollback/cleanup behavior explicit during source import and deletion.

## Usage examples

No user-facing command changes are required. Existing flows continue to use the same source lifecycle commands:

```bash
coral source add --file path/to/source.yaml
coral source test <source>
coral sql "select * from <source>.<table>"
```

Existing credential material remains under `workspaces/<workspace>/sources/<source>/secrets.env`.

## Validation

- `git diff --check $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`
- `cargo test -p coral-app`
- `make rust-checks`

feat(engine): expose search metadata catalog (#312)

Expose search/retrieval metadata through SQL catalog surfaces.

Why this metadata exists:
- The source spec now has provider-native search functions and bounded search behavior, but generic agents/tools cannot reliably use those semantics if they only exist in source YAML or prose docs.
- This metadata makes the retrieval contract queryable through the catalog: agents can ask what search functions exist, how to call them, what limits apply, which result columns come back, and which filters are available for follow-up table queries.
- This is the catalog layer needed by mechanical discovery flows such as `list_catalog` / `search_catalog`, without hardcoding provider-specific knowledge or relying on prose.
- Detail-hint catalog exposure is intentionally deferred: existing migrated sources are unambiguous enough through search result ids plus catalog-described tables, while the source-spec support can remain available for future providers with thinner or more ambiguous search results.

Changes:
- Adds `kind`, `arguments_json`, `result_columns_json`, and `search_limits_json` to `coral.table_functions`.
- Adds `search_limits_json` to `coral.tables`.
- Adds normalized `coral.filters` metadata, including filter type, mode, and descriptions.
- Exposes nullable `coral.columns.filter_mode` for columns that correspond to declared filters.

build(cli): make embedded UI build explicit (#658)

## Intent

This is an alternative to #646 that keeps the embedded UI enabled as the default CLI surface without making Cargo or `build.rs` run npm.

The design split is:
- Cargo compiles the embedded UI code path by default.
- Local Rust builds may compile without `ui/dist`; UI development normally serves assets from Vite.
- Make/CI own UI artifact generation and validation.
- Release/install paths build the UI before packaging the CLI.

## Shape

- Enables `coral-cli`'s default `embedded-ui` feature.
- Leaves `rust-embed` tolerant of missing local `ui/dist` so Rust checks do not depend on frontend artifacts.
- Keeps `build.rs` limited to rebuild hints and embedded version metadata; it does not invoke npm or validate UI artifacts.
- Adds `make ui-build`, validates `ui/dist/index.html`, and makes `make install` build UI first.
- Restores `make rust-checks` to `--all-features`.
- Updates CI UI build paths to run `npm ci`, build the UI, verify `ui/dist/index.html`, and reject mock-only code in production output.
- Pins UI Node selection with `ui/.node-version`; UI release builds now require that file.

## Validation

- `cargo check -p coral-cli --all-targets --all-features --locked` with `ui/dist` temporarily hidden
- `make ui-build`
- production mock-code grep from `validate.yml`
- `npm run test:ui:type-check --prefix ui`
- `make rust-checks`
- `git diff --check`

feat(engine): execute Notion search as table function (#352)

## Summary
- Migrates Notion's real provider search surface to the executable source-scoped table function `notion.search_objects(query => ...)`.
- Uses Notion's API argument name `query` and binds it to the `/v1/search` request body.
- Adds `kind: search` and `search_limits` for the Notion provider search function.
- Keeps the legacy `notion.search` table as a deprecated compatibility surface and points its guide to the new function.
- Updates the HTTP engine fixture so function tests exercise `kind: search` plus `search_limits`.

## Syntax
```sql
SELECT object, id, url, public_url
FROM notion.search_objects(query => 'Coral')
LIMIT 10;
```

Use returned ids with the catalog-described Notion tables when full details are needed, for example:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM notion.pages
WHERE page_id = '<returned id>';
```

feat(mcp): add MCP-backed source support (#402)

## Summary

Adds a new `backend: mcp` source type so Coral can expose MCP tools as
SQL
tables and source-scoped table functions.

This PR includes:

- `coral-spec` manifest parsing, JSON schema support, and validation for
MCP
  sources.
- `coral-engine` runtime support for stdio MCP servers through `rmcp`.
- Tool-backed SQL tables with filter pushdown into MCP tool arguments.
- Source-scoped table functions with named SQL arguments.
- Shared JSON response row extraction for HTTP and MCP backends.
- Structured MCP query errors for missing filters/args, server startup,
  initialization, tool call, tool-returned error, and decode failures.
- A community ClickHouse Cloud MCP source under
  `sources/community/clickhouse_mcp`.

No public source-spec docs are included yet.

## Manifest Shape

MCP sources declare a stdio server command plus tables and/or functions.

```yaml
dsl_version: 3
name: clickhouse_mcp
version: 0.1.0
backend: mcp

server:
  transport: stdio
  command: npx
  args:
    - -y
    - mcp-remote
    - https://mcp.clickhouse.cloud/mcp
```

### Tables

Tables are for stable collection-shaped tool calls.

```yaml
tables:
  - name: services
    tool: get_services_list
    filters:
      - name: organization_id
        required: true
        tool_arg: organizationId
    response:
      rows_path: [result]
    columns:
      - name: organization_id
        type: Utf8
        virtual: true
        expr:
          kind: from_filter
          key: organization_id
      - name: id
        type: Utf8
        nullable: false
      - name: name
        type: Utf8
        nullable: false
```

Query:

```sql
SELECT id, name, state
FROM clickhouse_mcp.services
WHERE organization_id = 'org_123';
```

The table provider extracts supported equality filters from DataFusion,
serializes them into MCP tool arguments, calls the tool, extracts rows
with
`ResponseSpec`, and converts JSON rows to Arrow through `JsonExec`.

Tables can also opt into pushing SQL `LIMIT` into a tool argument:

```yaml
limit_binding:
  tool_arg: page_size
  max: 200
```

The engine still applies the row cap after extraction, so
`limit_binding`
improves upstream efficiency without changing SQL semantics.

### Table Functions

Functions are for operation-shaped calls where explicit invocation
arguments
are clearer than table filters.

```yaml
functions:
  - name: run_select_query
    tool: run_select_query
    args:
      - name: query
        required: true
        bind:
          arg: query
      - name: service_id
        required: true
        bind:
          arg: serviceId
    response:
      rows_path: [result, data]
    columns:
      - name: row
        type: Json
        expr:
          kind: current_row
```

Query:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM clickhouse_mcp.run_select_query(
  query => 'SELECT database, name FROM system.tables LIMIT 10',
  service_id => 'svc_123'
);
```

Function arguments must be named. The engine validates required
arguments
before planning the scan.

## Key Decisions

### MCP-specific manifest names, shared binding semantics

MCP table manifests use MCP-native names like `tool_args`,
`filters[].tool_arg`, and `limit_binding.tool_arg`. They do not expose
HTTP
request vocabulary such as query params, body fields, headers, or
routes.

Internally, MCP reuses the same lower-level concepts where they are
generic:

- source input/value rendering through `resolve_value_source`
- SQL filter extraction through the shared filter helper
- JSON row mapping through `convert_items`
- Arrow execution through `JsonExec`

### Tables and functions both matter

Tables make collection-shaped tools easy to query and join:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM clickhouse_mcp.service_backups
WHERE organization_id = 'org_123' AND service_id = 'svc_123';
```

Functions make operation-shaped tools explicit:

```sql
SELECT *
FROM clickhouse_mcp.get_service_details(
  organization_id => 'org_123',
  service_id => 'svc_123'
);
```

The backend supports both instead of forcing every MCP tool into one SQL
shape.

### Avoid backend duplication

HTTP and MCP both produce JSON payloads. This PR moves row extraction
into
`backends/shared/response_rows.rs` so `Direct`, `DictEntries`, and
`SeriesPointList` behavior stays consistent across JSON-producing
backends.

The intended boundary is:

1. Backend-specific code fetches one JSON payload.
2. Shared `ResponseSpec` logic extracts rows.
3. Shared mapping/execution code produces Arrow batches.

MCP does not reuse HTTP request structs because those carry HTTP-only
concepts.

### Static manifest contract

The engine does not introspect MCP tools at query time. The manifest
remains
the contract for SQL names, filters, arguments, response shape, and
columns.

Tool/schema introspection is left for a future scaffolding workflow.

## Error Handling

MCP errors now flow through structured query errors where possible:

- `MISSING_REQUIRED_FILTER`
- `MISSING_REQUIRED_FUNCTION_ARG`
- `MCP_SERVER_START_FAILED`
- `MCP_INITIALIZE_FAILED`
- `MCP_TOOL_CALL_FAILED`
- `MCP_TOOL_RETURNED_ERROR`
- `MCP_RESULT_DECODE_FAILED`

This gives CLI/MCP consumers stable error codes and metadata instead of
only
plain DataFusion error strings.

## ClickHouse MCP Source

Adds `sources/community/clickhouse_mcp` as the first real MCP source
example.
It uses `mcp-remote` to bridge Coral's stdio-only MCP runtime to the
remote
ClickHouse Cloud MCP endpoint.

The source exposes:

- Cloud management tables such as organizations, services, ClickPipes,
  backups, costs, databases, and tables.
- Functions for service details, private endpoint config, SQL execution,
and
  ClickPipe operations.

It lives under `sources/community` rather than `sources/core`, so it is
a
repo-distributed source and not bundled into the binary.

## Pending Work

- ~~Richer `LIMIT`/pagination pushdown beyond the initial
`limit_binding`
  support~~ 14954692836cf17fcd460661730d632d98149338
- ~~Better typed function argument serialization if MCP tools require
non-string
  arguments.~~ c0c06af3df5c2f5d3a7223ea53662198b8188db0
- Add telemetry
- Public docs for `backend: mcp` once the manifest shape is stable
enough.
- Real stdio MCP fixture/integration test that starts a child MCP
server.
- Support HTTP streaming
- Session- or source-scoped MCP process pooling if process startup
becomes
  material for repeated scans.
- MCP resource and resource-template backed tables.
- Optional scaffolding from `tools/list`, `inputSchema`, and
`outputSchema`.

## Validation

Recommended validation before merging:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps --locked
```

Targeted areas covered by tests in this branch:

- MCP manifest parsing and validation.
- MCP tables and functions in the engine.
- Required table filters and required function args.
- Filter pushdown into MCP tool args.
- Projection and limit behavior.
- `limit_binding` behavior.
- MCP catalog metadata.
- Shared response row extraction.
- Structured MCP error mapping.

ci(release): promote release after artifact upload (#690)

## Summary

- Configure release-please to create GitHub releases as prereleases.
- Promote the GitHub release to a full release only after release artifacts and checksums have uploaded.
- Trigger the Homebrew tap bump only when a release is promoted, while still allowing manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuilds to refresh tap checksums.
- Remove the standalone Discord release workflow and send the release announcement from the release workflow after promotion.

## Why

This addresses the issue where `scripts/install.sh` can fail while the release pipeline is running. The installer asks GitHub for the latest full release, but the release previously became latest before the binaries and `checksums.sha256` were available. Publishing the release as a prerelease keeps `/releases/latest` on the previous complete release until assets are attached.

## Validation

- `jq empty release-please-config.json`
- Ruby YAML parse for `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `git diff --check`

Not run: the release workflow itself.

feat(sources/community/vercel): add Vercel community source (#434)

## Summary

Adds a new community source for Vercel under
`sources/community/vercel/`.

This source enables querying Vercel platform data (projects,
deployments, domains, environment variables, and team members) through
SQL using the Vercel REST API. The source is manifest-only, read-only,
and uses Coral's existing HTTP source-spec model. No CLI, MCP, config,
or runtime changes.

Closes #433

## What changed

Added:

- `sources/community/vercel/manifest.yaml`
- `sources/community/vercel/README.md`

## Tables

| Table | Endpoint | Pagination | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projects` | `GET /v10/projects` | `cursor_query` | Supports `search`,
`repo`, `repo_id` filters |
| `deployments` | `GET /v6/deployments` | `cursor_query` | Supports
`project_id`, `state`, `target` filters |
| `domains` | `GET /v5/domains` | `cursor_query` | All domains for the
account/team |
| `environment_variables` | `GET /v10/projects/{id}/env` | `none` |
Requires `project_id` filter; returns all env vars in one response |
| `team_members` | `GET /v3/teams/{id}/members` | `cursor_query` |
Requires `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` input |

## Auth

Bearer token via `Authorization: Bearer <VERCEL_TOKEN>`.

Inputs:

- `VERCEL_TOKEN` — required secret, created at
https://vercel.com/account/tokens
- `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` — optional variable (default: `""`) for team-scoped
queries. Personal-account users can leave this empty.

## Implementation notes

**Pagination**
- Projects, deployments, domains, team members use Vercel's cursor-based
pagination (`pagination.next` in response → `from`, `until`, or `since`
query param), mapped to Coral's `cursor_query` mode.
- Environment variables use `mode: none` — the Vercel API returns all
env vars for a project in a single response with no pagination support
(`limit`/`since` are not documented query params).

**Response mapping**
- Environment variables return an object containing an array under the
`envs` key (`rows_path: [envs]`).
- Other endpoints return rows under named keys (`projects`,
`deployments`, `domains`, `members`).

**Columns**
- Rate-limit headers (`X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`) are
declared.
- Commonly queried nested fields are flattened with double-underscore
naming (`creator__username`, `creator__email`).
- Complex nested payloads (`link`, `meta`, `alias`, `target`,
`project_settings`, `joined_from`) are kept as Json columns.
- Timestamps use `format_timestamp` with `milliseconds` input to match
Vercel's epoch-ms format.
- `teamId` query param is injected from `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` input on all
endpoints that support it.
- Team member columns match the current v3 API response shape: `uid`,
`email`, `username`, `name`, `role`, `avatar`, `created_at`,
`confirmed`, `access_requested_at`, `joined_from`.

## Validation

- `coral source lint` — passes
- `make lint-sources` (`ryl`) — passes
- `git diff --check` — passes
- **Live query validation** — successfully completed against a real
Vercel account. `coral source test` passes for all 5 tables. Schema
mappings and cursor pagination logic behave correctly under live loads,

feat(sources/community/neo4j): add Neo4j community source (#552)

Closes #551

## What changed

Adds a community source for Neo4j under `sources/community/neo4j/`.

**Tables (6):**
- `node_labels` - all node labels defined in the database; start here
for graph discovery
- `relationship_types` - all relationship types defined in the database
- `nodes` - generic node table filtered by label; returns `element_id`,
`labels` (JSON array), and `properties` (JSON object) — works with any
graph schema
- `relationships` - graph edges with `from_element_id`, `from_label`,
`rel_type`, `rel_properties`, `to_element_id`, and `to_label`;
filterable in SQL via `rel_type`
- `indexes` - all indexes with `name`, `type`, `state`, `entity_type`,
`labels_or_types`, and indexed properties
- `constraints` - all constraints with `name`, `type`, `entity_type`,
`labels_or_types`, and constrained properties

**Auth:**
- HTTP Basic auth via `NEO4J_USERNAME` and `NEO4J_PASSWORD`
- Base URL configured via `NEO4J_URL` (default: `http://localhost:7474`)
- Target database configured via `NEO4J_DATABASE` (default: `neo4j`)
- Uses Neo4j HTTP transactional API: `/db/<NEO4J_DATABASE>/tx/commit`

**How it works:**
- Neo4j's transactional HTTP API returns Cypher results as positional
arrays (`results[0].data[N].row[N]`) rather than named objects
- Each Cypher query uses `COLLECT({key: value, ...})` to produce
named-key objects that Coral can navigate via string-key traversal in
`rows_path` and column `expr` paths
- The `nodes` table passes the label filter as a Cypher `$parameter` via
`WHERE any(l IN labels(n) WHERE l = $label)` to avoid Cypher injection
through identifier interpolation

## Why it changed

Neo4j is one of the most widely adopted graph databases for
relationship-heavy data modeling, knowledge graphs, recommendation
systems, fraud detection, and connected data workflows. Being able to
query graph topology, node inventories, relationship mappings, indexes,
and constraints through SQL is a natural fit for Coral.

The source is designed to work against any Neo4j graph - not a specific
domain schema. The `nodes` table accepts any label as a filter and
returns all properties as a JSON object, so users can query their own
graph without modifying the manifest.

## Local setup

Start Neo4j:

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name neo4j \
  -p 7474:7474 \
  -p 7687:7687 \
  -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo4j/password \
  neo4j:latest
```

Neo4j Browser: `http://localhost:7474` — username `neo4j`, password
`password`.

Add the source:

```bash
export NEO4J_URL=http://localhost:7474
export NEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j
export NEO4J_PASSWORD=password
coral source add --file sources/community/neo4j/manifest.yaml
```

A sample graph with Users, Organizations, Products, Orders, and
Technologies (with indexes and constraints) is included in the README as
a tutorial for testing.

- `coral source add --file` - connected successfully, 6 tables
- `coral source test neo4j` - 2 declared · 2 passed · 0 failed
- All 6 tables queried against a live Neo4j 5.x instance with sample
data
- `nodes` table queried with multiple label filters (`User`,
`Organization`, `Product`)
- `relationships` table filtered by `rel_type`

- `manifest.yaml` - source spec with 6 generic tables
- `README.md` - setup guide, sample data tutorial, example queries

## Summary
Adds a community source spec for [n8n](https://n8n.io) — the workflow
automation platform.

Closes #680

## Tables
- `workflows` — automation workflows with name, description,
active/archived status, trigger count, tags, project, settings, and
timestamps
- `executions` — execution runs with status, mode, finished flag,
timing, and retry metadata

- **Read-only.** `includeData=false` on executions to keep payloads
small.

execution IDs as `type: number`, but we use `Utf8` so
`executions.workflow_id` can join cleanly against `workflows.id` (which
the API returns as a string). Coral coerces JSON numbers to strings when
the column type is `Utf8`.
- **No `executions_by_workflow` function.** Removed per reviewer
feedback — `SELECT ... FROM n8n.executions WHERE workflow_id = 'X'`
provides the same functionality via the table + filter.
- **`N8N_BASE_URL` is `required: true`** with no default, so users must
supply their instance URL explicitly.
- **`N8N_API_KEY` is `kind: secret`** per repo rules for credential
inputs.

|---|---|
| `workflows` | `active`, `tags`, `name`, `project_id` |
| `executions` | `status`, `workflow_id`, `project_id` |

enabling users to query public posts, pages, tags, and authors via the

relation details by default.

functions.

fix(install): make checksum verification resilient (#742)

## Summary
- Replace the release checksum pipeline with explicit `sha256sum` calls
for tarballs and zip archives, restoring bare filenames in
`checksums.sha256`
- Make `install.sh` find the checksum entry by fixed-string archive name
instead of depending on two spaces plus an exact bare filename
- Add explicit GitHub REST headers and optional
`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` authentication when present to latest version
detection
- Add a `Validate` workflow job that runs the local install script
through `sh < scripts/install.sh` on every supported Unix
OS/architecture target
- In CI, pass `${{ github.token }}` to that install-script job to avoid
unauthenticated `api.github.com` 403s from GitHub-hosted runner IP pools
- Record in `AGENTS.md` that installer changes must keep that validation
matrix in sync

## Problem
PR #663 changed checksum generation to use `find . ... | xargs
sha256sum`, which made `checksums.sha256` contain entries like
`./coral-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`.

The installer still grepped for entries ending in two spaces plus the
bare archive name, like `coral-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`. With
the `./` prefix present, the grep produced no checksum line and
`sha256sum -c -` failed with `standard input: no properly formatted
checksum lines found`. This broke the `curl -fsSL
https://withcoral.com/install.sh | sh` install path for Linux release
artifacts.

## CI follow-up
The install-script matrix exposed macOS CI failures while fetching
`https://api.github.com/repos/withcoral/coral/releases/latest`: the API
returned HTTP 403 before archive download or checksum verification. This
matches [reports](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/42748)
of unauthenticated `api.github.com` calls from GitHub Actions
intermittently failing from shared hosted runner pools. The CI job now
passes `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the installer remains unauthenticated by default
for users.

After rebasing onto current `origin/main`, docs freshness also required
regenerating `docs/reference/community-sources.mdx` for the newly merged
Google Drive community source.

## Validation behavior changed
When `scripts/install.sh` or the validation workflow changes, CI now
runs the install script on:
- `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` via `ubuntu-24.04`
- `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` via `ubuntu-24.04-arm`
- `x86_64-apple-darwin` via `macos-15-intel`
- `aarch64-apple-darwin` via `macos-15`

## Testing
- Validated that generated checksum entries use bare archive filenames
- Validated installer checksum verification against both bare and
`./`-prefixed checksum entries
- Ran `sh -n scripts/install.sh`
- Parsed `.github/workflows/validate.yml` with Ruby YAML
- Ran a full local unauthenticated install-script smoke test on
`aarch64-apple-darwin`
- Ran `env RUSTC_WRAPPER= make docs-check`
- Ran `git diff --check`

feat(sources/community/k8s): add kubernetes community source (#420)

Closes #414

Summary

Adds a new read-only community Kubernetes source under:

sources/community/k8s/

This source enables querying Kubernetes cluster resources, workload metadata, networking objects, storage entities, operational events, and cluster infrastructure metadata through SQL using the Kubernetes API server.

The source is designed primarily for OSS/self-managed Kubernetes clusters. v1 targets local and shared development through kubectl proxy, with optional support for API base URLs that already inject authentication through a reverse proxy or gateway.

Tables

Table | Description -- | -- pods | Pod metadata, lifecycle state, scheduling, node placement, container status deployments | Deployment metadata including replicas, availability, selectors, labels replicasets | ReplicaSet ownership and scaling metadata statefulsets | Stateful workload replica state daemonsets | Node-level workload scheduling and rollout metadata jobs | Batch job execution and completion state cronjobs | Scheduled job configuration and execution scheduling services | Cluster networking services, ports, selectors, exposure ingresses | Ingress routing rules, host configuration, load-balancing endpoints | Service endpoint subsets for service-to-backend mapping networkpolicies | Network policy selectors and policy types persistentvolumeclaims | Persistent storage claim metadata and binding state events | Cluster events for debugging and lifecycle triage (with first_timestamp / last_timestamp / count / action) configmaps | Configuration metadata serviceaccounts | ServiceAccount metadata nodes | Node-level infrastructure, kubelet version, labels

The nodes table is cluster-scoped and always requires cluster-wide list nodes.

A minimal read-only ClusterRole is documented in sources/community/k8s/README.md under "RBAC requirements".

Pushdown filters

All namespace-scoped tables support:

  • label_selector → Kubernetes labelSelector

  • field_selector → Kubernetes fieldSelector

  • namespace → rewrites the request to the namespaced list URL

Pagination and result safety

  • Kubernetes API pages are handled via continue-token chunking (cursor_query pagination mode).

  • Every table sets fetch_limit_default: 500 as a total-row safety cap so a naive SELECT * FROM k8s.pods cannot accidentally scan an entire large cluster. SQL LIMIT and pushdown filters are still important for large clusters; the README explains this in the "Total-row safety cap (fetch_limit_default) vs Kubernetes limit" section.

Why it changed

Kubernetes clusters generate large amounts of operational metadata across workloads, scheduling, networking, storage, infrastructure, orchestration state, and operational events.

Teams frequently need answers to operational questions such as:

  • Which pods are not running?

  • Which deployments are unhealthy?

  • Which PVCs are pending?

  • Which recent warning events explain a failure?

Without a Coral source, users typically need to inspect cluster state with kubectl, write custom scripts, or aggregate metadata externally. This source makes Kubernetes operational metadata directly queryable through SQL for operational analytics, debugging workflows, infrastructure visibility, and automation systems.

What was tested

  • coral source lint sources/community/k8s/manifest.yaml — manifest validation passed

  • make lint-sources — validation passed

  • coral source add --file … + coral source test k8s — validated against a live kind cluster via kubectl proxy

  • All 16 tables queried successfully with expected schema mapping

  • Cluster-wide and namespace-scoped request variants both exercised

  • Kubernetes continue-token pagination handling verified

  • Event timing (first_timestamp / last_timestamp) and count columns verified parsing as Timestamp / Int64 from real /api/v1/events payload

Declared test queries (all pass)

✓ SELECT
namespace, name, status FROM k8s.pods LIMIT 20
✓ SELECT namespace, name, replicas, available_replicas FROM
k8s.deployments LIMIT 10
✓ SELECT namespace, object_name, reason, message, last_timestamp, count
    FROM k8s.events WHERE object_kind = 'Pod'
    ORDER BY last_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20
✓ SELECT name, status FROM k8s.pods WHERE namespace = 'kube-system'
LIMIT 10

The fourth test exercises the namespaced request variant (/api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/pods); the third exercises the new event timing/count columns.

Example queries

Failing pods (namespace-scoped, namespace-RBAC friendly)

SELECT namespace, name, status, status_reason
FROM k8s.pods
WHERE namespace = 'production'
  AND status != 'Running'
LIMIT 20;

Recent warning events

SELECT namespace, object_kind, object_name, reason,
message,
       last_timestamp, count
FROM k8s.events
WHERE type = 'Warning'
ORDER BY last_timestamp DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 20;

Unhealthy deployments

SELECT namespace, name, replicas,
available_replicas
FROM k8s.deployments
WHERE replicas != available_replicas
LIMIT 50;

Pending PVCs

SELECT namespace, name, phase, storage_class
FROM k8s.persistentvolumeclaims
WHERE phase = 'Pending'
LIMIT 20;

User-visible impact

New k8s source installable via:

kubectl proxy --port=8080
export K8S_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080
coral source add --file
sources/community/k8s/manifest.yaml

Notes

  • Read-only v1 (no mutating Kubernetes API calls)

  • Uses the standard Kubernetes API surface exposed through kubectl proxy or a pre-authenticated base URL

  • Supports label_selector, field_selector, and namespace pushdown on list tables

  • Nested Kubernetes resource payloads are preserved as Json where appropriate

  • ISO 8601 timestamp fields (pod startTime, event timestamps) are parsed via format_timestamp(iso8601) so they're true Coral Timestamp columns

Follow-on

Potential future additions:

  • Bearer-token or client-certificate authentication for direct API server access

  • namespaces and persistentvolumes tables

  • secrets support with careful redaction

  • horizontalpodautoscalers, resourcequotas, limitranges, ingressclasses

  • Cluster usage metrics integration

  • Workload relationship mapping

  • Helm release metadata

Filtered queries preserve completeness (no silent cap); use a pushdown predicate or an explicit LIMIT N to bound. Adds a new read-only community Prometheus source under
`sources/community/prometheus/`.

v1 sends Prometheus’s native `limit` parameter on instant queries,
exposes typed
sample values and timestamps, and intentionally excludes an
arbitrary-PromQL
table until per-result-type handling is complete.

## Tables

| --- | --- |
| `query_up` | Scrape health (PromQL `up`, server-side `limit=500`) |

## Files

Tables:

feat(sources/community/auth0): add Auth0 community source (#719)

Closes #715

# Summary

Adds a new community source for Auth0 under `sources/community/auth0/`.

This source exposes Auth0 tenant configuration, applications, user
directories, identity provider connections, and audit log metadata
through Coral, enabling SQL-based querying for identity and access
management (IAM) reporting, security auditing, and configuration
management.

---

# Tables Added (15)

## Identity & Users
- `auth0.users` — Full user directory including profiles, logins count,
and provider-side search via the `q` filter.

## Applications & APIs
- `auth0.clients` — Application (client) inventory including callbacks,
allowed origins, and JWT settings.
- `auth0.resource_servers` — APIs registered in the tenant with scopes
and token configuration.
- `auth0.connections` — Identity provider connections (database, social,
enterprise, etc).

## Access Control & Authorization
- `auth0.roles` — RBAC role definitions.
- `auth0.role_users` — Users assigned to specific roles.
- `auth0.role_permissions` — Permissions granted to specific roles.
- `auth0.client_grants` — Authorized scopes for machine-to-machine
clients.
- `auth0.grants` — Authorizations given by users to applications.

## Tenant Architecture
- `auth0.organizations` — Organizations configured in the B2B tenant.
- `auth0.organization_members` — Members within specific organizations.
- `auth0.actions` — Serverless pipeline actions.
- `auth0.custom_domains` — Custom domains configured for the tenant.
- `auth0.tenant_settings` — Global tenant settings (returned as a single
row).

## Audit & Telemetry
- `auth0.logs` — Tenant log events (authentication attempts, signups,
API ops). Supports `q` filter (Lucene query syntax).

---

# Authentication

Uses API token authentication via:

```bash
AUTH0_API_TOKEN
```

Sent using the:

```text
Authorization: Bearer 
```

request header.

API tokens can be generated from the Auth0 Dashboard under `Applications
> APIs > Auth0 Management API` (API Explorer) or via a Client
Credentials grant.

The source configures dynamic routing to the tenant domain via:

```bash
AUTH0_DOMAIN
```

(e.g., `https://dev-abc123.us.auth0.com`).

---

# Why This Change

Auth0 is one of the most widely used Identity as a Service (IDaaS)
platforms.

Exposing Auth0 infrastructure metadata through Coral enables teams to:
- Audit IAM configuration and RBAC policies.
- Track application and API scopes.
- Monitor authentication events and anomalous log activity.
- Verify user directory state.
- Build operational visibility dashboards for security compliance using
standard SQL.

This is especially valuable for security engineering, IAM governance,
and compliance reporting.

---

# What Was Tested

## Validation

```bash
coral source lint sources/community/auth0/manifest.yaml
```
Passes cleanly. YAML syntax is valid and all 15 tables load properly.

## Source Registration

```bash
export AUTH0_DOMAIN="https://dev-abc123.us.auth0.com"
export AUTH0_API_TOKEN="..."
coral source add --file sources/community/auth0/manifest.yaml
```
Connected successfully and registered all 15 tables.

## Integration Testing

`test_queries` verified successfully against a live Auth0 tenant:
```sql
SELECT user_id, email, name FROM auth0.users LIMIT 1
```

---

# User-visible Impact

Users can now install and query Auth0 directly through Coral.

Example:

```bash
export AUTH0_DOMAIN="https://dev-abc123.us.auth0.com"
export AUTH0_API_TOKEN=""

coral source add --file sources/community/auth0/manifest.yaml
coral sql "SELECT user_id, email, name, logins_count FROM auth0.users ORDER BY last_login DESC LIMIT 20;"
```

feat(sources/community/bitbucket): add bitbucket community source (#744)

Fixes [#736](https://github.com/withcoral/coral/issues/736)

Add a new `bitbucket` community source that lets Coral query Bitbucket
Cloud
repositories, pull requests, and CI/CD pipelines through SQL — enabling
PR
cycle-time analytics, deployment tracking, compliance reporting, and
cross-source joins with the bundled Jira source.

This change is manifest-only and uses Coral's existing HTTP source-spec
model
with the OAuth 2.0 authorization-code credential block. Read-only. No
CLI,
MCP, config, or runtime changes.

## What changed

Added:

- `sources/community/bitbucket/manifest.yaml`
- `sources/community/bitbucket/README.md`

## Source scope

Inputs:

- `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` — OAuth access token (secret), collected via browser
OAuth flow or manual paste
- `BITBUCKET_CLIENT_ID` — Bitbucket OAuth consumer Key (variable),
required to initiate the OAuth flow; non-secret app identifier
- `BITBUCKET_CLIENT_SECRET` — Bitbucket OAuth consumer Secret (secret),
required for confidential-client token exchange

OAuth:

- Flow: `authorization_code` with `pkce: disabled` (Bitbucket Cloud
requires a confidential client with `client_secret`; PKCE public-client
flow is not currently supported)
- Redirect URI: `http://127.0.0.1:53682/oauth/callback`
- Authorization URL: `https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/authorize`
- Token URL: `https://bitbucket.org/site/oauth2/access_token`
- Scopes: `account repository pullrequest pipeline`
- Client secret transport: `basic_auth`

Tables:

- `bitbucket.repositories`
  - `GET /repositories/{{filter.workspace}}`
  - required filter: `workspace`
  - page pagination (`page` / `pagelen`), page size up to 100
- 9 columns: `slug`, `name`, `description`, `language`, `size`,
`is_private`, `created_on`, `updated_on`, `workspace`
- `slug` is the value to pass as `repo_slug` in `pull_requests` and
`pipelines`

- `bitbucket.pull_requests`
- `GET
/repositories/{{filter.workspace}}/{{filter.repo_slug}}/pullrequests`
  - required filters: `workspace`, `repo_slug`
  - page pagination (`page` / `pagelen`), page size up to 100
- 11 columns: `id`, `title`, `description`, `state`, `author_nickname`,
`source_branch`, `destination_branch`, `created_on`, `updated_on`,
`workspace`, `repo_slug`
  - `state` values: `OPEN`, `MERGED`, `DECLINED`, `SUPERSEDED`

- `bitbucket.pipelines`
- `GET
/repositories/{{filter.workspace}}/{{filter.repo_slug}}/pipelines`
  - required filters: `workspace`, `repo_slug`
  - page pagination (`page` / `pagelen`), page size up to 100
- 9 columns: `uuid`, `build_number`, `state_name`, `state_result_name`,
`creator_nickname`, `created_on`, `completed_on`, `workspace`,
`repo_slug`
- `state_name` examples: `COMPLETED`, `IN_PROGRESS`; `state_result_name`
examples: `SUCCESSFUL`, `FAILED`

## Implementation notes

- `auth`: `Authorization: Bearer {{input.BITBUCKET_TOKEN}}` via
`HeaderAuth`
- All three tables use `rows_path: [values]` — the Bitbucket Cloud REST
API v2.0 wraps paginated results in a `values` array
- All three tables use `mode: page` pagination with `page_param: page`,
`page_start: 1`, `page_step: 1`, `query_param: pagelen`
- `workspace` and `repo_slug` filter values are echoed onto every row as
`virtual: true` columns via `from_filter`
- `state_name` and `state_result_name` in `pipelines` are sourced from
nested `state.name` and `state.result.name` API fields;
`author_nickname` in `pull_requests` from `author.nickname`;
`source_branch` and `destination_branch` from `source.branch.name` and
`destination.branch.name`
- `BITBUCKET_CLIENT_ID` is `kind: variable` (non-secret app identifier);
`BITBUCKET_CLIENT_SECRET` is `kind: secret`
- Bitbucket Cloud does not expose a workspace-discovery endpoint without
admin scopes; `workspace` is therefore a required filter on all tables,
matching the behaviour of the bundled Jira and Confluence sources

## Out of scope

Not included in v1:

- Workspace discovery (requires admin scopes not appropriate for a
read-only source)
- `commits` table
- `branches` table
- Pipeline steps and log output
- Write operations of any kind

feat(sources/community/typeform): add Typeform community source (#604)

## What this does

This adds a new community source for
[Typeform](https://www.typeform.com/) a popular form and survey
platform. It lets you query your Typeform account data using SQL through
Coral.

## Tables

The source exposes **5 tables**:

- **`forms`** — All forms in your account. Supports filtering by
workspace and text search. Includes public URL, visibility status, and
timestamps.
- **`workspaces`** — Workspaces that organize your forms. Includes form
counts so you can see workspace sizes at a glance.
- **`themes`** — Visual themes (colors, fonts, backgrounds) used by your
forms. Useful for design auditing.
- **`responses`** — Submitted responses for a given form. Includes
answers (as queryable JSON), quiz scores, hidden fields, and respondent
metadata like browser and platform.
- **`webhooks`** — Webhook subscriptions configured on a form. Shows
destination URLs, enabled/disabled status, and SSL verification
settings.

## Authentication

Uses a single Personal Access Token (`TYPEFORM_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`,
`kind: secret`), sent as a Bearer token. Users generate this from their
Typeform account settings.

## design decisions

**No configurable base URL** : Typeform is a SaaS-only product with no
self-hosted option, so the base URL is hardcoded to
`https://api.typeform.com`.

**Responses fetch up to 1000 per request** : The Typeform Responses API
uses cursor-based pagination where the cursor is the `token` field of
the last response item. This pattern can't be expressed via
`response_cursor_path` in the source-spec DSL (which expects a fixed
path in the response body, not a value from the last array element). As
a pragmatic workaround, the source requests the API maximum of 1000
responses per call, and provides `since`, `until`, and `query` filters
so users can slice larger datasets by time window.

**Webhook secrets intentionally omitted** : The Typeform webhooks API
returns a `secret` field used for HMAC payload signing. This is excluded
from the schema since it's a sensitive credential.

**answers column typed as `Json`** : This enables users to extract
individual answer values with `json_get_str`, `json_get_int`, and other
JSON accessor functions.

## Validation

```
$ cargo run -p coral-cli -- source lint sources/community/typeform/manifest.yaml
Manifest is valid
```

feat(sources): Add Trello Community Source (#763)

Fixes #762.

### Summary

This PR adds a community source spec for **Trello**, exposing boards,
lists, cards, and members as SQL-queryable tables via the Trello REST
API. Authentication is implemented using the standard API key and token
query parameters.

### Motivation

Trello is a highly popular visual work management tool. Integrating
Trello into Coral allows users to query their project management data
directly via SQL, unlocking a wealth of project tracking and analytics
capabilities.

### Credential Overview

Trello uses a dual-parameter authentication approach involving an API
Key and a User API Token. These are passed as `key` and `token` query
parameters on every request.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Credentials Setup | [Trello Power-Up
Admin](https://trello.com/power-ups/admin) |
| Client inputs | `TRELLO_API_KEY` (variable) + `TRELLO_API_TOKEN`
(secret) |
| Allowed Origins | `http://localhost` (or `*`) for manual token
generation |

### Table Schema

| Table | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `boards` | `GET /1/members/me/boards` | All boards the authenticated
user belongs to |
| `lists` | `GET /1/boards/{board_id}/lists` | All lists (columns) on a
specific board (requires `board_id`) |
| `cards` | `GET /1/boards/{board_id}/cards` | All cards on a specific
board (requires `board_id`) |
| `members` | `GET /1/boards/{board_id}/members` | All members on a
specific board (requires `board_id`) |

### Example SQL Queries

```sql
-- Join cards with their corresponding list names
SELECT
  c.name AS card_name,
  l.name AS list_name,
  c.due
FROM trello.cards c
JOIN trello.lists l ON c.list_id = l.id
WHERE c.board_id = 'YOUR_BOARD_ID'
  AND l.board_id = 'YOUR_BOARD_ID';
```

| Format | JSON (`fmt=json`) |

docs: clarify OAuth source spec authoring (#691)

## Intent

Make OAuth-backed source-spec authoring clear now that OAuth credential retrieval is supported. The previous custom-source guide still framed browser-based auth as outside the ideal source model, and the maintained source-spec skills did not teach agents how to author or review OAuth credential methods.

## What It Enables

- Source spec developers can see when OAuth-backed APIs are a good fit.
- The source-spec reference now explains that `credential.methods` controls setup while `auth` still controls runtime requests.
- The create/review skills now guide agents through OAuth credential method authoring, validation, and review checks.
- Future credential-retrieval guidance changes have a durable AGENTS rule to keep docs and skills aligned.

## Usage Examples

For a provider that supports browser-based setup, define `credential.methods` on the stored token secret:

```yaml
inputs:
  DEMO_API_TOKEN:
    kind: secret
    credential:
      methods:
        - type: oauth
          label: Connect with Demo
          oauth:
            flow:
              type: authorization_code
              pkce: required
            redirect_uri: http://127.0.0.1:0/oauth/callback
            redirect_uri_port_mode: random
            endpoints:
              authorization_url: https://demo.example.com/oauth/authorize
              token_url: https://demo.example.com/oauth/token
            client:
              id:
                input: DEMO_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
        - type: source_config
          label: Paste token
auth:
  type: HeaderAuth
  headers:
    - name: Authorization
      from: template
      template: Bearer {{input.DEMO_API_TOKEN}}
```

Then run:

```sh
coral source add --interactive --file ./my-source.yaml
```

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- `git diff --cached --check`
- `cargo test -p coral-spec oauth`
- `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- export-skills --dest /private/tmp/coral-skills-export`

`cargo run --locked -p coral-cli -- source lint /private/tmp/coral-oauth-doc-snippet.yaml` was attempted but hit sandboxed `sccache` permissions before approval could complete; the parser-level OAuth tests and skill export check passed.

﻿## Summary

Closes #833.

This source lets Coral query a local LM Studio OpenAI-compatible server
for visible models, bounded non-streaming Responses API checks, bounded
single-turn chat-completion checks, and embedding vectors through SQL.

## Why this source

LM Studio is a popular local model runtime for testing LLMs on a
workstation. Coral does not currently include an LM Studio source under
`sources/community` or `sources/core`, so this community source adds a
focused SQL surface for local LLM workflows.

This source helps users:

- Discover models visible to the LM Studio OpenAI-compatible server.
- Run bounded Responses API and single-turn chat-completion checks
through SQL.
- Generate embedding vectors from an embedding-capable local model.
- Join local model inventory with other Coral sources during agent or
workflow debugging.

The first version is intentionally narrow. It uses LM Studio's
documented OpenAI-compatible endpoints and avoids model-detail path
lookups so model IDs containing `/` remain safe.

## Provider docs

- LM Studio local server: https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/server
- LM Studio API quickstart:
https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/rest/quickstart
- LM Studio authentication:
https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/authentication

https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat/models

https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat/responses
